warnings: KNOWN GATE CASE RESOLVED: master's existing warnings (and op_fix SKILL.md history) flag หน้า12 (A-10, 'แบบขยายแปลนห้องน้ำ') as referencing grid_ref 'A-B x 1-1'' when the master has no '1'' line — this is the house-11-bathroom case op_fix's gridfix.py ERROR gate expects. Read the หน้า12 image directly: it prints a real '2.30' dimension from the room's west outer-wall face to grid '1' (top of the plan, single grid-1 bubble, no second bubble on that edge), matching the canonical 'offset before grid 1' example in spec §4. Transcribed as dimension_chains x-axis {from:'@-2.3', to:'1', value_m:2.3} — NOT resolved to the name '1'' myself (naming/prime-sequencing is gridfix.py's job per op_fix), but this is exactly the printed dimension that should let gridfix.py create a line at pos_m -2.30 and match it to the existing 'A-B x 1-1'' ref without an ERROR gate. Flagging explicitly per the task brief rather than assuming success.

THREE DIFFERENT west-of-grid-1 offsets found on three different pages, kept separate rather than merged — every one is a genuinely different printed value, and nothing here proves they describe the same wall: หน้า12 (WC bathroom west wall) = 2.30 west of grid 1 (@-2.3); หน้า22 (small B1/B5 utility-room appendage, ชานพัก zone) = 1.65 west of grid 1 (@-1.65); หน้า15 (ramp-plan bedroom wall nib, row C) = 0.65 west of grid 1 (@-0.65). All three read cleanly off single, unambiguous ticks anchored to the same known grid-1 bubble, so all three are recorded as separate dimension_chains rows. Whether gridfix.py's within-0.05m same-point merge collapses any pair, or whether a human needs to confirm these are three genuinely staggered wall lines in that west appendage, is left for review — not guessed here.

หน้า15/หน้า16 (ทางลาดเอียง R.1, 'แบบขยายทางลาดเอียง' detail sheets, pattern=section): the master's own warnings/non_grid_dimensions_do_not_confuse say this ramp/landing/เฉลียง zone is 'slab-only, no dummy grid created' — that predates the 2026-09-27 rule-4 update. Both sheets print REAL grid bubbles (1,2,3 / C,D) matching the known grid exactly (4.00/3.00 x; 2.00 y reprint on หน้า16's รูปตัด1/รูปตัด2), so per the current rule 4 ('it doesn't matter... which kind of sheet printed it — plan, side_profile, section, roof') any dimension printed FROM one of those known lines TO an unlabelled edge was swept, not skipped: หน้า15 gives 0.65 west of grid 1 (bedroom wall nib, row C), 1.00/1.50/2.00 south of row C (landing step edges — 2.00 also confirms known C-D), and 1.70 south of row D (south edge of the ramp, beyond the already-known D' at 10.30 — this is a NEW point at @10.7, further south than D' — flagging this explicitly since it means the ramp footprint extends past the dummy line the master already carries for the C0 footings). หน้า16's cleaner section view gives one new point: D + 0.40 = @9.4 (เฉลียง floor-edge nosing, y-axis). Several OTHER printed numbers on หน้า15 (a cluster of 0.10/1.10 reveals near the grid-2 post, 1.90/0.30 near the handrail example-line callout, 3.20 overall width at the sheet's bottom) could not be traced to a specific known-line anchor with confidence from the image at the resolution available — these went to unassigned_dimensions rather than being guessed into a chain; a closer human read of หน้า15 (ideally at full native resolution/paper) could probably resolve them.

หน้า22 (S-04, แปลนเสา คาน พื้น ชั้นที่ 1) — two genuinely new points beyond the three west-of-grid-1 items above: (1) the B4A beam's own JSON already flagged 'printed 1.65 offset east of grid 2' (grid_ref_end 'A-3(partial)') — confirmed visually, the '1.65' dimension's left tick sits directly under grid 2, giving a new x-point @5.65 (row A, toward the SX slab marker). (2) the small B1/B5 appendage room's north edge is 1.35 south of row C (@8.35) — a NEW y-point, distinct from หน้า15's 1.00/1.50 (@8.0/@8.5) and หน้า23's 1.11 (@8.11) found on the ring-beam sheet for the same general appendage/B6X-stub zone. These four y-values (1.00, 1.35, 1.50, 1.11 — all measured south of row C) almost certainly describe different corners/edges of the small appendage room and its B6X stub beam as drawn on different sheets at different scales/purposes, not a single point read four different ways — recorded as four separate points rather than merged or discarded, per the 'nothing gets dropped for not fitting a category' rule. A human (or gridfix.py's 0.05m merge check) should sanity-check whether any of these four coincide.

หน้า23 (S-05, แปลนคานระดับอะเส) — one more new x-point: grid 1 + 3.50 = @3.5 at row A (a printed 'X.XX' style offset shorter than the full 4.00 to grid 2; its exact associated feature — possibly a CS steel-column position — was not confidently identified from the image, but the dimension itself reads clearly off grid 1, so it is recorded). One new y-point: row C + 1.11 = @8.11 (the B6X stub beam's north end, per the file's own pre-existing warning 'B6X ... west of grid 1 near row C — offsets 1.11/1.50 printed'). The companion '1.50' on the same sheet (spacing between the two B6 roof-support posts south of row C, near the small gable ridge from หน้า07's @8.05) could NOT be confidently anchored to a specific known line from the image at the resolution available — both its ends looked close to, but not exactly on, the B6 column centrelines — so it was left in unassigned_dimensions rather than guessed.

D' (the dummy y-line south of D, already in the master at pos_m 10.30, carrying the two southern C0/F1 isolated footings) still has NO printed x-dimension for its own x-position on any page swept this pass — this matches the master's and หน้า20/21's own existing confidence_flags ('x-position of the D' pair flagged low-confidence since no x-dimension was printed for them specifically, only the 1.65m spacing between the pair'). Nothing new found here; not fabricated.

The four isolated C0 footings (north of A at A', south of D at D') remain functionally unexplained by anything read this pass (matching every prior sheet's same open question, carried since S-02/S-03) — no new sheet swept this round (05/06/07/08/09/10/12/15/16/20/21/22/23/24/37/44) resolves what superstructure they support. This is a large house (64 distinct source pages excluding the master, ~86 json files since several BOQ pages split into _1/_2). Pages 45-66 are entirely material_list (BOQ) tables with zero dimension rows — verified by pattern field + spot-checking sheet_name text, not by opening every one of the ~44 BOQ json files' images (would be reading tables, not drawings, per the task's own 'be efficient' instruction). All other non-axis-bearing pages (schedules, index/symbol pages, notes, and every member-level detail/cross-section sheet: door-window schedule, WC fixture-height/grab-rail standards, footing/beam/slab/precast/seismic detail sheets, pipe-installation details, panel schedule) were skipped per the reasons logged in pages_skipped — each checked against its own JSON's pattern/sheet_name/content (and the image directly for the roof-eave detail หน้า17 and the WC/ramp cluster หน้า12/13/15/16, since those were judgement calls, not mechanical pattern matches).
